description: This topic covers essential plant nutrients, the roles and deficiency symptoms of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, organic manures, inorganic fertilizers, and methods of fertilizer application.

mcq.questionText: Which group of nutrients is required by plants in large amounts?
mcq.explanation: Macronutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are needed by plants in relatively large quantities.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a primary macronutrient for plants?
mcq.explanation: Nitrogen is one of the three primary macronutrients, together with phosphorus and potassium.

mcq.questionText: Yellowing of older leaves in a maize plant is most likely a sign of deficiency of which nutrient?
mcq.explanation: Nitrogen deficiency causes chlorosis (yellowing), starting with the older lower leaves because nitrogen is moved to younger growth.

mcq.questionText: Which nutrient is mainly responsible for promoting strong root development and early ripening of crops?
mcq.explanation: Phosphorus encourages good root growth and helps crops to ripen and mature earlier.

mcq.questionText: A fertilizer that supplies only nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium together is called a:
mcq.explanation: A compound fertilizer such as NPK contains more than one nutrient element in a single product.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an organic manure?
mcq.explanation: Farmyard manure is made from animal dung, urine and bedding, making it an organic manure.

mcq.questionText: Which fertilizer has the highest percentage of nitrogen and is commonly used in Tanzania?
mcq.explanation: Urea contains about 46% nitrogen, the highest of the common nitrogenous fertilizers.

mcq.questionText: Green manure is best described as:

options.text: Dried animal dung spread on the soil
Fresh green plants ploughed into the soil to add nutrients
Crushed rock added to the soil

mcq.explanation: Green manure is made by growing leguminous or leafy plants and ploughing them into the soil while still green.

mcq.questionText: Applying fertilizer in a band or furrow before or at planting is known as:
mcq.explanation: In band placement the fertilizer is placed in rows near the seeds or roots so the crop can use it efficiently.

mcq.questionText: Spraying a dissolved fertilizer directly onto the leaves of a crop is called:
mcq.explanation: Foliar application supplies nutrients quickly through the leaves and is useful for correcting micronutrient deficiencies.

mcq.questionText: Which nutrient deficiency causes scorching or browning at the edges of leaves and weak stems?
mcq.explanation: Potassium deficiency typically shows as scorching or yellowing along leaf margins and results in weak stems.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of organic manure over inorganic fertilizer?

options.text: It supplies nutrients in an exact known amount
It improves soil structure and water-holding capacity
It acts very quickly within a few days
It is light and easy to transport in small bags

mcq.explanation: Organic manure adds humus that improves soil structure, aeration and the ability of the soil to hold water.

mcq.questionText: One disadvantage of inorganic (artificial) fertilizers is that:

options.text: They contain too few nutrients to be useful
They can make the soil acidic if overused
They always improve soil humus content
They are too bulky to carry to the farm

mcq.explanation: Continuous heavy use of some inorganic fertilizers can lower soil pH and make the soil acidic.

mcq.questionText: Which micronutrient is required by plants in only very small amounts?
mcq.explanation: Zinc is a micronutrient (trace element) needed by plants in very small quantities.

mcq.questionText: Why is fertilizer often applied as top dressing some weeks after planting rather than all at once?

options.text: To make the work last longer for the farmer
To supply nutrients when the growing crop needs them and reduce loss by leaching
Because fertilizer cannot be applied at planting time
To make the soil more acidic

mcq.explanation: Top dressing supplies nutrients during active growth and reduces nutrient losses that would occur if all fertilizer were applied early.

fib.questionText: Nutrients needed by plants in large quantities are called _____.
fib.explanation: Macronutrients include nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

fib.questionText: The nitrogenous fertilizer with about 46% nitrogen is called _____.
fib.explanation: Urea is the most concentrated common nitrogen fertilizer.

fib.questionText: The yellowing of leaves due to lack of chlorophyll is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Chlorosis is a common symptom of nitrogen deficiency.

fib.questionText: Manure made by rotting plant and animal remains in a pit or heap is called _____.
fib.explanation: Compost is formed by the decomposition of organic materials.

fib.questionText: The nutrient that promotes strong root growth and early ripening of crops is _____.
fib.explanation: Phosphorus is important for root development, flowering and ripening.

fib.questionText: Spreading fertilizer evenly over the whole field by hand or machine is called _____.
fib.explanation: Broadcasting distributes fertilizer over the entire soil surface.

fib.questionText: Fresh green plants that are ploughed into the soil to improve fertility are known as _____.
fib.explanation: Green manure crops are often legumes that add nitrogen to the soil.

fib.questionText: Manure made from animal dung, urine and bedding materials is called _____.
fib.explanation: Farmyard manure is collected from livestock housing and added to the soil.

fib.questionText: A fertilizer that supplies only one nutrient element is called a _____ fertilizer.
fib.explanation: A straight fertilizer such as urea provides a single nutrient.

fib.questionText: Applying fertilizer to a crop after it has already started growing is called _____.
fib.explanation: Top dressing supplies extra nutrients during active crop growth.

tf.questionText: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are the three primary macronutrients of plants.
tf.explanation: These three are the main nutrients supplied in NPK fertilizers.

tf.questionText: Micronutrients are required by plants in very large amounts.
tf.explanation: Micronutrients such as zinc and iron are needed only in very small amounts.

tf.questionText: Nitrogen deficiency usually causes yellowing of the older, lower leaves first.
tf.explanation: Nitrogen is mobile and moves from old leaves to new growth, so older leaves yellow first.

tf.questionText: Phosphorus helps to delay ripening and weakens plant roots.
tf.explanation: Phosphorus actually promotes strong roots and encourages early ripening.

tf.questionText: Compost and farmyard manure are examples of organic manures.
tf.explanation: Both are made from decomposed plant and animal materials.

tf.questionText: Inorganic fertilizers generally act faster than organic manures.
tf.explanation: Inorganic fertilizers release nutrients quickly because they are already in soluble forms.

tf.questionText: Organic manure improves the structure and water-holding capacity of the soil.
tf.explanation: The humus from organic manure improves soil structure, aeration and moisture retention.

tf.questionText: Foliar application means burying fertilizer deep below the plant roots.
tf.explanation: Foliar application means spraying dissolved fertilizer onto the leaves.

tf.questionText: Overuse of some inorganic fertilizers can make the soil acidic.
tf.explanation: Continuous heavy application of certain fertilizers lowers soil pH over time.

tf.questionText: A compound fertilizer contains only a single nutrient element.
tf.explanation: A compound fertilizer such as NPK contains two or more nutrient elements.

summary.questionText: Two groups of essential plant nutrients
summary.explanation: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and micronutrients in small amounts.
These are supplied together in NPK compound fertilizers.

summary.questionText: Main role of nitrogen in plants
summary.correctAnswer: Promotes leaf and vegetative growth and green colour
summary.explanation: Nitrogen is part of chlorophyll and proteins, giving healthy green leaves.

summary.questionText: Main role of phosphorus in plants
summary.correctAnswer: Encourages root growth, flowering and ripening
summary.explanation: Phosphorus supports strong roots and early maturity of crops.

summary.questionText: Main role of potassium in plants
summary.correctAnswer: Strengthens stems and improves disease resistance
summary.explanation: Potassium helps plants resist disease and improves quality of fruits and tubers.

summary.correctAnswer: Yellowing (chlorosis) of older leaves and stunted growth
summary.explanation: Lack of nitrogen reduces chlorophyll and slows growth.

summary.correctAnswer: Farmyard manure, compost and green manure
summary.explanation: All are made from decomposed plant or animal materials.

summary.correctAnswer: Urea, sulphate of ammonia and superphosphate
summary.explanation: These are factory-made fertilizers supplying specific nutrients.

summary.correctAnswer: Broadcasting, band placement, top dressing and foliar spraying
summary.explanation: The method chosen depends on the crop, fertilizer and growth stage.

summary.questionText: Main advantage of organic manure over inorganic fertilizer
summary.correctAnswer: It improves soil structure and adds humus
summary.explanation: Organic manure improves aeration, water retention and long-term fertility.

hoq.questionText: A farmer notices that the older lower leaves of his maize are turning yellow while the soil is sandy and was not manured. Which combination best explains and solves the problem?

options.text: Potassium deficiency, solved by adding lime
Nitrogen deficiency, solved by top dressing with a nitrogen fertilizer such as urea
Excess phosphorus, solved by removing topsoil
Too much water, solved by adding more fertilizer

hoq.explanation: Yellowing of older leaves on poor sandy soil points to nitrogen deficiency, which is best corrected by top dressing with a nitrogen fertilizer.

hoq.questionText: Why might a farmer who relies only on inorganic fertilizers for many years eventually get poorer yields even though nutrients are added?

options.text: Inorganic fertilizers add no nutrients at all
The soil loses humus and structure and may become acidic, reducing its ability to support the crop
Inorganic fertilizers make the soil hold too much water
Plants stop needing nutrients after a few years

hoq.explanation: Without organic matter the soil loses humus and structure and can become acidic, so nutrients alone cannot maintain good yields.

hoq.questionText: A farmer wants to correct a micronutrient deficiency quickly without changing the whole soil. Which method and reason is most appropriate?

options.text: Broadcasting farmyard manure, because it releases micronutrients instantly
Foliar spraying, because nutrients enter through the leaves and act quickly
Deep ploughing, because it removes the deficiency
Adding more seeds, because new plants will not be deficient

hoq.explanation: Foliar spraying delivers small amounts of nutrients directly through the leaves, making it the fastest way to correct micronutrient deficiencies.
